# claude-memsync command reference

<!-- GENERATED by scripts/gen-reference.sh from the binary's --help output. Do not edit by hand; CI fails when this file is stale. -->

Every section is the verbatim output of the command shown. For what the commands do and when to use them, see [setup.md](setup.md), [security.md](security.md) and [claude-memsync.md](claude-memsync.md).

## `claude-memsync --help`

```text
claude-memsync — sync Claude Code memories across workstations

Usage:
  claude-memsync <subcommand> [args]

Subcommands:
  init        Bootstrap the local sync repo against a remote
  doctor      Check every mem-* repo in the org is private (--org, --install-timer)
  app         app register: create a GitHub App through the manifest flow
  app-token   Print a GitHub App installation token (--app <name>) for use as another tool's token command
  repo        repo create <name>: create a private mem-* repo and verify it
  run         Run the sync daemon in the foreground
  distill     Rebuild the distilled-memory catalog index (see --prune, --dry-run)
  archive     List or search the archive of deleted notes (archive list, archive search <term>)
  route       Edit routing: the home folder, publish or inherit a host template
  changes     List memory files changed in the sync repo since a commit (for hooks)
  relate      Declare a read or join relation between two memory repos (registry)
  unrelate    Remove a relation
  related     List relations; "related sync" fetches read clones, "related context" prints a session index, "related suggest" offers edges from this host's data
  recipients  add | remove | list | accept the age recipients of an encrypted repo
  join        join request|status|list|accept|reject: add a new host as an age recipient of an existing repo
  host        list | check-key: the machines that share these repos (deploy keys, recipients, expiry)
  install     Install as a system service (Windows Service / systemd unit / launchd plist)
  uninstall   Remove the system service
  start       Start the system service
  stop        Stop the system service
  status      Report service status
  version     Print version
  help        Show this help
```

## `claude-memsync init -h`

```text
Usage of init:
  -archive-deletes
    	archive instead of delete: a note removed from a Claude folder moves to archive/ in the repo (sets archiveDeletes in config.json)
  -claude-dir string
    	override Claude projects directory (default: ~/.claude/projects)
  -denylist string
    	UTF-8 file of regexes (one per line) to install as the denylist before the first commit
  -encrypt
    	encrypt every file in the repo with age (new or already-encrypted remotes only)
  -encryption-scheme string
    	with --encrypt: pq (hybrid post-quantum age keys only, the default) or classic (upstream-compatible X25519/ssh keys); saved as encryptionScheme (default "pq")
  -expires string
    	last day this host syncs (YYYY-MM-DD); the day after, the daemon holds and status says to retire it; saved to config and published to the registry
  -force
    	re-init even if sync-dir already exists
  -github-api-url string
    	GitHub API base URL (GitHub Enterprise); saved to config
  -github-app string
    	apps.json entry to mint the GitHub token from (see app-token); saved to config; not with --token-cmd
  -github-host string
    	git host remotes must use (default github.com); saved to config
  -host-label string
    	a name you choose for this host (such as laptop-2): titles its deploy keys, labels its age recipient, names it in the registry; saved to config
  -identity string
    	with --encrypt: age identity file (default: identity.txt in the claude-memsync config dir, $XDG_CONFIG_HOME or ~/.config, or in the older OS config dir if the file is already there; generated if missing)
  -ignore-foreign-writers
    	go on although a foreignWriters entry is active or cannot be checked (logged)
  -private-only
    	enforce private mem-* repos only (name allowlist + GitHub visibility checks); saved to config
  -read-only
    	read-only member: pull and apply notes into the Claude tree, never commit or push (the remote must already hold the repo); saved to config
  -recipient value
    	with --encrypt: extra age/ssh public key, e.g. an offline recovery key (repeatable)
  -recovery-recipient value
    	with --encrypt: the owner's offline recovery key (an age1pq1... public key under the pq scheme, repeatable): a recipient like --recipient, marked "# recovery", saved as recoveryRecipients, and the only kind of recipient "join accept" lets go unlabelled
  -remote string
    	git remote URL to sync against (e.g. git@github.com:user/claude-memories.git)
  -skip-quiet-window
    	skip the start-up quiet window
  -sync-dir string
    	override sync work-tree (default: ~/.claudesync)
  -token-cmd string
    	command (shell-style quotes, no shell) printing a GitHub token, e.g. "gh auth token"; saved as githubTokenCmd (the command, never the token); not with --github-app
  -token-file string
    	file holding a GitHub token for the private-only check (or set MEMSYNC_GITHUB_TOKEN)
```

## `claude-memsync doctor -h`

```text
Usage of doctor:
  -config string
    	path to config.json
  -github-app string
    	apps.json entry to mint the GitHub token from, for this run; not saved
  -install-timer
    	write a daily user timer (systemd) or launchd agent for doctor; does not enable it
  -org string
    	GitHub org to check (default: config githubOrg, else owner of the remote)
  -routes string
    	path to routes.json: check every repo it routes (default: as for run, unless --config is given)
  -token-cmd string
    	command (shell-style quotes, no shell) printing a GitHub token, e.g. "gh auth token"; run at call time, never saved
  -token-file string
    	file holding a GitHub token for this run (as for init; or set MEMSYNC_GITHUB_TOKEN); not saved
  -unit-dir string
    	with --install-timer: directory to write units into
```

## `claude-memsync app`

```text
usage:
  claude-memsync app key-fingerprint --key-file <pem>
  claude-memsync app add --name <n> --app-id <id> --org <org> (--key-cmd "<cmd>" | --key-file <path>) [--api-url <url>] [--replace] [--verify]
  claude-memsync app register --name <n> --org <org> --url <homepage> --perm <p:level>... (--key-out <path> | --key-cmd-store "<cmd>" --key-cmd "<cmd>")
```

## `claude-memsync app add -h`

```text
Usage of app add:
  -api-url string
    	GitHub API base URL (default: public GitHub); recorded as apiBase
  -app-id string
    	numeric GitHub App ID (required)
  -apps-file string
    	apps.json path (default: ~/.config/claude-memsync/apps.json)
  -key-cmd string
    	command that prints the private key (shell-style quotes, no shell)
  -key-file string
    	private key file (mode 0600, yours, one hard link)
  -name string
    	apps.json entry name (required)
  -org string
    	org the app is installed on (required)
  -replace
    	overwrite an existing entry with this name
  -verify
    	mint a token against the org to prove the entry works (prints MINT-OK)
```

## `claude-memsync app register -h`

```text
Usage of app register:
  -api-url string
    	GitHub API base URL (default: public GitHub; for Enterprise); recorded as apiBase in apps.json
  -apps-file string
    	apps.json path (default: ~/.config/claude-memsync/apps.json)
  -github-url string
    	GitHub web base URL (default https://github.com; for Enterprise)
  -key-cmd string
    	with --key-cmd-store: the command that prints the stored key, recorded in apps.json (shell-style quotes, no shell)
  -key-cmd-store string
    	command that reads the private key on stdin and stores it (shell-style quotes, no shell)
  -key-out string
    	write the private key to this new file (mode 0600; refused if it exists)
  -name string
    	GitHub App name; also the apps.json entry name (required)
  -org string
    	org that will own the app (required)
  -perm value
    	app permission <name>:<read|write|admin> (repeatable)
  -url string
    	homepage URL recorded in the app manifest (required)
```


## `claude-memsync run -h`

```text
Usage of run:
```

## `claude-memsync distill -h`

```text
Usage of distill:
  -config string
    	path to config.json (default: ~/.claudesync/config.json)
  -dry-run
    	report what would change without writing the index or pruning
  -prune
    	remove catalog entries whose source memory lost the marker or vanished (archived instead when archiveDeletes is on)
  -repo string
    	with a routes file: the repo to rebuild (a key of routes.json repos; default: the personal repo)
  -routes string
    	path to routes.json (default: $CLAUDE_MEMSYNC_ROUTES, then ~/.config/claude-memsync/routes.json if it exists)
```

```text
usage:
  claude-memsync archive list [--since YYYY-MM-DD] [--repo name | --config path] [--routes path]
```

```text
Usage of archive list:
  -config string
    	path to config.json (default: ~/.claudesync/config.json)
  -repo string
    	with a routes file: read only this repo (a key of routes.json repos)
```

## `claude-memsync route`

```text
usage:
  claude-memsync route home [<repo>|deny] [--folder F] [--yes] [--confirm-move-out-of-client]
  claude-memsync route home --unpin | --suggest | --ask
  claude-memsync route publish --as <label> [--registry DIR]
  claude-memsync route inherit <label> [--home] [--yes] [--confirm-move-out-of-client] [--registry DIR]
all take --routes <file>
```

## `claude-memsync route home -h`

```text
Usage of route home:
  -ask
    	choose interactively (needs a terminal)
  -confirm-move-out-of-client
    	allow taking the home folder out of a client or orch repo
  -folder string
    	home folder name (default: from $HOME)
  -routes string
    	routes file
  -suggest
    	print a suggested choice and the reason; changes nothing
  -unpin
    	remove the home pin (the folder then routes by the other rules)
  -yes
    	confirm non-interactively: pins a repo with no prompt; never replaces --confirm-move-out-of-client (a client/orch repo involved still refuses)
```

## `claude-memsync route inherit -h`

```text
Usage of route inherit:

  -registry string

  -routes string

  -yes

```

## `claude-memsync changes -h`

```text
Usage of changes:
  -config string
    	path to config.json (default: ~/.claudesync/config.json)
  -deadline duration
    	with --hook: give up after this long, print nothing and move no marker (0 = none; $CLAUDE_MEMSYNC_HOOK_DEADLINE_MS, in ms, sets the default) (default 1.5s)
  -hook
    	run as a Claude Code hook: read its JSON from stdin, keep a per-session marker, print additionalContext JSON
  -json
    	print JSON instead of text
  -limit int
    	list at most N changes, then "...N more" (0 = no limit) (default 20)
  -marker string
    	file whose first line is the base commit (this or --since is required)
  -project string
    	only this project: a project directory, or Claude's folder name for it
  -routes string
    	with --hook: path to routes.json, to report across several repos (default: $CLAUDE_MEMSYNC_ROUTES, then ~/.config/claude-memsync/routes.json if it exists)
  -since string
    	git revision to compare HEAD with (this or --marker is required)
  -synced
    	compare with the commit last copied into ~/.claude (.state/synced-head) instead of HEAD
  -update-marker
    	with --marker, rewrite the file to the current HEAD afterwards (a missing or stale marker only records the baseline)
```

## `claude-memsync recipients`

```text
usage: claude-memsync recipients add <public-key> [--host <label>] | remove <public-key> | list | accept --yes | label self --host <label> | label recovery <public-key> [--all] | rekey-pq --recovery-recipient <age1pq1...> --host <label> [--all] [--fresh-root] [--apply] | rekey-pq (--repo <name> | --all) --rollback [--discard-local-commits] | rekey-pq --drop-backup | retire-classic [--all] [--apply]  [--repo <name> | --config <path>] [--routes <path>]
```

## `claude-memsync join`

```text
usage:
  claude-memsync join request --repo <name> --label <host-label>   (on the new host)
  claude-memsync join status [--repo <name>]                       (on the new host; lists each key with its label)
  claude-memsync join list [--repo <name>]                         (on a member host; shows each request's label)
  claude-memsync join accept <label> --repo <name> --fingerprint <fp> [--allow-unlabelled]
  claude-memsync join reject <label> [--repo <name>]
  (repo selection as for recipients: --repo <key-or-GitHub-repo-name> | --config <path>, --routes <path>)
```

## `claude-memsync join request -h`

```text
Usage of join request:
  -allow-unlabelled
    	accept: admit even though some recipient has no host label (label it first with "recipients label self")
  -fingerprint string
    	accept: the fingerprint the requesting host printed
  -label string
    	host label (^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{0,31}$)
```
